items.excerpt: # Hermes Agent ☤ Hermes Agent | Hermes Desktop **The self-improving AI agent built by [Nous Research](https://nousresearch.com).** It's the only agent with a built-in learning loop — it creates skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge, searches its own past conversations, and builds a deepening model of who you are across sessions. Run it on a $5 VPS, a GPU cluster, or serverless infrastructure that costs nearly nothing when idle. It's not tied to your laptop — talk to it from Telegram while it works on a cloud VM. Use any model you want — [Nous Portal](https://portal.nousresearch.com), OpenRouter, OpenAI, your own endpoint, and [many others](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers). Switch with `hermes model` — no code changes, no lock-in. A real terminal interface Full TUI with multiline editing, slash-command autocomplete, conversation history, interrupt-and-redirect, and streaming tool output. Lives where you do Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and CLI — all from a single gateway process. Voice memo transcription, cross-platform conversation continuity. A closed learning loop Agent-curated memory with periodic nudges. Autonomous skill creation after complex tasks. Skills self-improve during use. items.title: BMAD's Founder on the Future of AI Coding (And the Slop Apocalypse)
items.summary: There's a slop apocalypse coming, and it's not broken AI generated code crashing everything in production. It's the quiet kind: comments drift out of sync with what the code actually does, nobody goes back and refactors what the agent wrote, and over time that's what makes the coding agent slower and more expensive to work with (the real failure mode). That's Brian Madison's read on where AI coding is headed, and a couple days ago I sat down with him to dig into it - why "human on the loop" beats full automation, what's coming in BMAD v7, and how his framework and my own landed on almost the same philosophy independently.
